## Hybrid Retrieval

Hybrid retrieval combines sparse lexical search (e.g. BM25) with dense vector search, then merges the two ranked result sets—often via reciprocal rank fusion—to capture both exact term matches and semantic similarity.

### Why Hybrid Retrieval?

Hybrid retrieval consistently outperforms either method alone, particularly on queries that mix:
- Rare identifiers (error codes, product SKUs)
- Natural language intent

This dual coverage addresses the complementary strengths of the two approaches: sparse methods excel at exact matches for domain-specific tokens, while dense vector search captures semantic relationships and paraphrasing.

### Production Adoption

Hybrid retrieval has become the default retrieval pattern in production RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems, reflecting its practical superiority over single-method approaches.

### Merging Strategy

Reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) is a common technique for merging the ranked result sets from sparse and dense methods, balancing the contributions of both signals without requiring manual weighting.
